description: Target the launch-bound serialized cuSOLVER geqr2 (77.9% of baseline) across the small/medium regime n in {32,176,352,512} (7 of 12 benchmark shapes). Write a custom CUDA C++ batched blocked Householder QR: one threadblock per matrix, stage ONLY the active column panel (e.g. 512x32, ~64KB) plus the WY/T reflector factors in shared memory while the trailing submatrix stays in global; do panel factorization and WY trailing update on-chip with no per-matrix kernel relaunch; emit compact (H,tau). Pure FP32 to lock the orthogonality/residual gates first. Route every other n to torch.geqrf.

Target the n in {1024,2048,4096} large-square regime (n=1024x60 shapes ~224ms each at baseline) where trailing-update GEMMs dominate. Write a custom CUDA C++ multi-block blocked Householder QR (panel width ~32-64): keep panel factorization and reflector norms/tau in FP32 for orthogonality, but cast the block-reflector trailing update A -= V*T^T*(V^T*A) to TF32/BF16 and run it on Blackwell tensor cores with FP32 accumulation. Exploit the ~2400x factor-residual and ~320x orthogonality margins. Route n not in {1024,2048,4096} to torch.geqrf for now.

Maximize throughput on the dominant n=512 batch=640 shapes (~80% of baseline cost; 4 benchmark cases incl. mixed/rankdef/clustered) with a precision-first custom CUDA QR: factor each matrix mostly in FP16/BF16 on tensor cores, then refine reflectors/factors back to FP32-accurate (H,tau) with correction pass(es). Single UNIFORM path for every matrix (no conditioning-based dispatch — the invariance guard forbids it). Binding constraint is the orthogonality gate (100*n*eps): measure the orthogonality margin every validate, not just the residual. torch.geqrf fallback for off-grid n.

Combine your n<=512 wide-block champion (37a1814b, 6.79x) with worker-1's large-n custom path (424096bf: n=1024 12.3x FP32, n=2048 2.93x TF32) into ONE submission that dispatches by n so every regime n in {32..2048} uses its best custom kernel; n=4096 and off-grid n stay on torch.geqrf. The 5 large-n shapes currently route to geqrf and dominate the geomean — coverage alone should reach ~15x. Hazards: keep BOTH load_inline modules with distinct names, preserve cuBLAS -lcublas linkage, and do NOT leak global TF32 allow_tf32 state across the n-regimes (the factor-residual gate trips if n=1024/2048's TF32 mode bleeds into another path).

Crack the low-batch large shapes n=4096 b=2 and n=2048 b=8, where one-threadblock-per-matrix starves the GPU (only 2-8 resident blocks on 100+ SMs) and they still sit near geqrf. Use INTRA-matrix panel parallelism: a multi-block-per-matrix panel factorization (cooperative-groups grid sync or a two-pass split-reduction across blocks), OR cuSOLVER's geqrf for just the panel via the current CUDA solver handle paired with your custom TF32/FP32 tensor-core strided-batched trailing update. n=2048 is genuinely compute-bound so tensor cores can pay there; keep FP32 where the factor-residual gate binds. Goal: both shapes well above 3x.

Push the three n=1024 b=60 shapes (incl mixed, nearrank) past worker-1's current 12.3x on this large-n base (424096bf). Apply your worker-0 expertise from the n<=512 line: warp-parallel geqr2 panel + parallel compact-WY T-build fully on-chip, occupancy tuning (ncu the panel kernel: it was the 1-block/SM shared-mem-bound limiter at n<=512), and wide blocks (one large trailing update per multi-subpanel block) to cut memory passes. Keep panel + reflectors FP32 (the factor-residual gate binds at n=1024 on nearrank, so TF32 trailing fails); the win is structural occupancy/launch, not precision.

On your 14.0x combine (9e8b4ca0), attack the SMALL-batch shapes that are occupancy-STARVED: n=32 b=20 is only 2.85x and n=352 b=40 only 11.8x because one-threadblock-per-matrix launches just 20/40 blocks on this 188-SM GPU. In geomean ratio-space these low-speedup shapes have the most leverage left, and no other worker owns them (W0=n1024, W1=n2048/4096). Pack MULTIPLE matrices per threadblock (e.g. warp-per-matrix or several small matrices co-resident per block) so the small/medium regime n in {32,176,352} saturates the SMs; tune the matrices-per-block and threads so 188 SMs stay busy at b=20..40. Keep the n>=512 dispatch untouched. FP32. Profile with ncu to confirm occupancy is the limiter.

On your 14.29x champion (fe3c3093), push the n=2048 b=8 shape — currently only 3.1x (24.5ms, TF32 nb=12), the worst-performing shape that is NOT at the occupancy wall (b=8 gives 8 matrices = real parallelism, and you found n=2048 is compute-bound). This is your strength: FP32 shared-memory panel geqr2 + a larger tensor-core (TF32/BF16, FP32-accumulate) strided-batched trailing GEMM. Tune the block width nb to push FLOPs into the tensor-core GEMM while holding the factor-residual gate (you saw TF32 trips ~12/20 on rankdef/nearrank at large n — find the nb/precision split that stays safe at b=8). Establish the true n=4096 b=2 ceiling (the one shape still on geqrf = the worst-ratio geomean term at 50.5ms) by trying the ONE contract-legal mechanism not yet attempted: RECURSIVE blocked-WY QR (Elmroth-Gustavson / LAPACK geqrt3 style). Recurse cols: factor left n/2 (down to small base panels), apply Q^T to the right half via large WY GEMMs (A12 -= V1 (T1^T (V1^T A12))), factor right n/2. tau = diag(T), V below diag, R upper -> the standard (H,tau), unlike TSQR. The bet: the big applies (top level 4096x2048x2048/matrix) are huge tensor-core GEMMs (FP32-accumulate; FP32 inputs since the 5e-3 factor gate bans TF32 on nearrank/rankdef), so even at b=2 they fill the 188 SMs and replace geqrf's SIMT-SGEMM trailing + sequential geqr2 panel with fewer/fatter TC launches. Parent is the champion fe3c3093 so you ONLY add the n=4096 path (n!=4096 dispatch untouched). If recursive QR can't beat geqrf's 50ms after honest effort, a clean 'geqrf is the floor for n=4096 b=2' finding is a valid return. Profile the applies with ncu.

Combine your faster n=1024 kernel (d7c9ff3b: two-level blocking + warp-parallel apply, ~21.5x on the three n=1024 b=60 shapes, up from 12.45x) INTO the current champion (fe3c3093, 14.29x). Both are the same blocked_qr family in submission.py, so this is a focused replacement of the n=1024 path/config, not a rewrite — keep the champion's n<=512 wide-block path, n=2048, n=4096, and off-grid dispatch byte-for-byte untouched. This directly lifts the global best by ~the n=1024 ratio gain. Validate all 3 guards; ncu only if a regression shows up.

Crack the n=2048 b=8 panel wall (3.1x) with RECURSIVE blocked-WY QR (Elmroth-Gustavson/geqrt3) — you proved n=2048's panel is the 50% bottleneck, work-bound on only 8 blocks/8 SMs, while the trailing is already tensor-core-bound. Recursive QR shrinks that sequential panel: recurse cols, factor left half down to small base panels, apply Q^T to the right via large WY GEMMs (A12 -= V1 (T1^T (V1^T A12))) on tensor cores (FP32-accumulate; FP32 inputs to hold the factor gate, your TF32 worstf was already ~6/20 so stay safe), factor right half. tau=diag(T), V below diag, R upper => standard (H,tau), unlike TSQR. The applies become big GEMMs that fill far more than 8 SMs even at b=8 — your trailing-GEMM strength. This is a DIFFERENT recursive target than worker-1's n=4096 b=2 (8 matrices = more parallelism, shallower recursion). Parent is the champion fe3c3093 so you ONLY touch the n=2048 path; keep all other dispatch untouched. If it can't beat 3.1x, that's a valid 'n=2048 panel is floor' finding. ncu the applies.

Kill the cuBLAS launch storm on the dominant shapes. Profiling the new champion (6dea562b) shows the n<=512 and n=1024 trailing/panel updates fragment into many tiny strided-batched cuBLAS GEMMs that emit ~11,897 splitKreduce launches + many small simt_sgemm tiles — pure launch/reduction OVERHEAD (not math- or occupancy-bound), hitting the highest-weighted n=512 b640 (x4) and n=1024 b60 (x3) shapes. Collapse it: enlarge the wide-block width / _SUBS so each trailing update is ONE larger GEMM (fewer launches), and/or replace the split-K-prone small V^T*trail and T^T*Y GEMMs with cublasLtMatmul configured to DISABLE split-K, or a single fused custom CUDA GEMM kernel. This is precision-neutral (FP32, factor/orth gates untouched -> safe on all conditioning incl rankdef/nearrank) and distinct from the recursive-QR work workers 1/2 are doing on n=2048/4096. Keep dispatch/correctness identical; target far fewer, larger launches. ncu/nsys to confirm the splitKreduce count drops and which shapes gain.

Restructure the n=1024 b=60 path (3 shapes = 25% of the geomean, banked at only ~21.5x vs n=512's 65x = the largest unclaimed headroom) into RECURSIVE blocked-WY QR so its trailing applies run on TF32 tensor cores SAFELY. Your n=4096 finding is the key: column-blocked TF32 trips the factor gate at n=1024 on nearrank (~15-20/20, why the current kernel is FP32), but the recursive-WY structure (FP32 base panels + Q^T applied in a few LARGE steps) keeps TF32 error from accumulating (you measured ~1.4/20, ~14x margin). Unlike n=4096 b=2, n=1024 has 60 matrices so the big TF32 GEMM applies actually pay (the panel isn't the sole bottleneck). Parent is the champion 6dea562b; add this as a distinct n=1024 module and route ONLY n=1024 to it, leaving n<=512/n=2048/n=4096/off-grid untouched. Pipeline the n=512 b=640 wide-block loop to overlap the panel factorization of block k+1 with the trailing update of block k — the four n=512 shapes are 4/12 of the geomean (biggest multiplicity lever) and your prior work optimized panel and trailing SEPARATELY but they still run SERIALLY per block. Look-ahead/double-buffer: while cuBLAS applies block k's wide trailing update to the right submatrix, factor block k+1's panel (which only needs block k's just-updated columns) concurrently — classic look-ahead blocked-QR latency hiding. Since the leaderboard bans explicit streams (the validate banned-construct scan rejects 'stream'), achieve overlap WITHIN the existing default-stream kernel structure: e.g. factor the next panel from the leading columns of the current trailing update inside one fused launch, or reorder so the panel kernel and trailing GEMM of adjacent blocks co-occupy the GPU. Keep n=2048/n=4096/off-grid dispatch untouched. Profile only if a knob's effect is non-obvious.

STRUCTURAL DEPARTURE for the dominant n=512 b640 shapes (4/12 geomean, our ceiling at ~15ms FP32): replace the latency-bound sequential Householder panel with CholeskyQR2 + Householder RECONSTRUCTION, which is BLAS-3 (square batched GEMMs) from step 1 so tensor cores are natural. Algorithm per matrix, fully batched: (1) G=A^T A (batched GEMM/SYRK, FP32 accumulate), (2) R=chol(G), (3) Q=A R^-1 (triangular solve), (4) repeat 1-3 once on Q = CholeskyQR2 (restores orthogonality for kappa up to ~u^-1/2), (5) RECONSTRUCT exact compact (H,tau) via Modified-LU of (Q - S), S=diag(sign): the Ballard-Demmel/Yamamoto lemma — running Householder QR on orthonormal Q == ModLU(Q-S), giving Householder vectors Y into H's strict-lower, R into upper, tau/T from a triangular solve (T^-1+T^-T = Y^T Y). KEY: the factor gate ||R-Q^T A|| passes because R is regenerated from the ORTHONORMAL Q (reconstruction is stable even for ill-conditioned A), defeating why naive TF32 trailing failed (24.7>20). Run the GEMMs in TF32/BF16 with FP32 accumulation for the tensor-core win. For extreme-kappa clustered/nearrank matrices that fail chol, fall back per-matrix to shifted CholeskyQR3 (G+sigma*I) or geqrf (shape-based fallback OK, NOT content-dispatch — apply uniformly or via chol-breakdown detection). This is the likely source of the leaders' 5x edge. Keep n!=512 dispatch untouched; off-grid->geqrf. All 3 guards; report worst-case factor+orth margins on mixed/rankdef/clustered.

Per matrix batched: (1) G=A^T A (batched GEMM, FP32 accumulate, TF32/BF16 inputs), (2) R=chol(G), (3) Q=A R^-1 (triangular solve), (4) repeat 1-3 once = CholeskyQR2 (restores orthogonality), (5) reconstruct exact compact (H,tau) via Modified-LU of (Q-S), S=diag(sign): Householder vectors Y into H strict-lower, R into upper, tau/T from triangular solve (T^-1+T^-T=Y^T Y). The factor gate ||R-Q^T A|| passes because R is regenerated from the ORTHONORMAL Q, so TF32/BF16 GEMMs are safe even on ill-conditioned inputs (defeats why the old TF32 trailing failed at n=2048). This is a CLEAN shape split: worker-0 is doing CholeskyQR2 on n=512 (hardest, smallest GEMMs), worker-1 recwy on n=1024 — you take n=2048 (easiest, biggest GEMMs); independent evidence across the n-range. Report the worst-case margin.

Attack n=4096 b=2 (our single worst shape, 1x/pure geqrf, drags the geomean hardest) by AMORTIZING the grid-sync barriers that capped worker-1's cooperative panel. That cuts syncs from ~4n to ~4n/b (~250 instead of 16,000, ~64x fewer barriers) while keeping all 188 SMs busy on the 2 matrices.
